### argparse scripts but in jupyter or ipython or VS Code etc

If I’m developing a CLI script in a notebook, I can’t just run it as a script because the notebook was already invoked _as_ a script.
Here is a simple one:

```python
def parse_args():
    """
    parse CLI args in a way that is robust to jupyter notebooks and scripts
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="experiment args")
    parser.add_argument(
        'N_c', type=int, nargs='?', default=10, help="Number of categories (default: 10)")

    known_args = parser.parse_known_args()[0]
    return vars(known_args)

def main(**args):
  # do stuff
    print(args)

if (
        __name__ == '__main__'  # if running as a script
        and 'get_ipython' not in dir()  # and not in jupyter notebook
        ):
    args = parse_args()
    main(**args)
```

## hydra

“[Hydra](https://hydra.cc/) is a framework for elegantly [configuring complex applications](./configuring_ml.qmd#).”
As a special case it [builds CLIs](https://hydra.cc/docs/tutorial/simple_cli) with autocomplete and other fun stuff.

## docopt

[docopt/docopt: Pythonic command line arguments parser, that will make you smile](https://github.com/docopt/docopt)

> docopt helps you:
>
> * define the interface for your command-line app, and
> * automatically generate a parser for it.
